Oxford: "The word originally meant 'to pawn or pledge something', later 'pledge oneself (to do something)', hence 'enter into a contract' (mid 16th cent.), 'involve oneself in an activity', 'enter into combat' (mid 17th cent.)"

立了约就得真的投入进去：投入活动是「参与、从事」，投入战斗是「交战」，把别人「约」进来做事是「雇用」（Etymonline 注此义出自『如被誓言绑住』的观念），让注意力被「绑住」则是「吸引」——四支都从「被约定缚住」生出。

给一个人「估价」估出高分，就是看重他：牛津指出此词曾比喻性地用来「评估人的长处」——评出的高价值转成了敬意（动词『看重』义 1530 年代见载，名词『敬重』义 1610 年代见载）。

semantic_path.how: 最早见载的意思
拉丁语的「估价」借进英语后先干本行：动词给物估价（1530 年代），名词就是估出来的价（1560 年代；1796 年起还专指建筑商的报价单）。
估出的价本来就不必分毫不差，「估个大概」从定价里松出来：名词 1580 年代已有「大致判断」义，动词 1660 年代有「形成粗略概念」义——词义从钱财估价扩大到一切大致推算。

mechanism_sentence 重写为『祸事本身 → 怕祸的心情』的机制。

Etymonline: "The sense of "state of being afraid, uneasiness caused by possible danger" developed by late 12c."
Etymonline: "The meaning "feeling of dread and reverence for God" is from c. 1400."

changes: original_meaning 保留拉丁语 fidelitas 的「忠实，忠诚」并与首站对齐（现行方向正确，仅 how 为套话）。
semantic_path 重建三站：按 Etymonline 编年补 1530 年代『忠于事实』义与 1878 年声音保真义，how 写明忠的对象如何从人扩到事实、再变成技术指标。
mechanism_sentence 重写。
evidence: Etymonline: "early 15c., "faithfulness, devotion," from Old French fidélité (15c.), from Latin fidelitatem... "faithfulness, adherence, trustiness," from fidelis "faithful"... from fides "faith""
Etymonline: "From 1530s as "faithful adherence to truth or reality;" specifically of sound reproduction from 1878."
fidelity.mechanism_sentence: fidelity 的根是 fides「信」：先是对人忠实，后来对事实忠实，最后连录音像不像原声，都要用它来量「忠不忠实」。

semantic_path.how: 最早见载的意思
「忠」的对象从人、信仰扩到事实本身：1530 年代起 fidelity 指对真相、原样的忠实贴合——复制、转述走不走样，也归它管（Etymonline 记此义 from 1530s）。

semantic_path.how: 海湾那副「隔开两边、跨不过去」的样子被搬到抽象事物上：1550 年代起 gulf 指观点、阶层之间宽阔得难以弥合的间隔（Etymonline 记此比喻义 from 1550s）。

changes: original_meaning 由义项并列改为 heardlice 的首要义「用力地，严厉地」。
semantic_path 按 Etymonline 编年重建四站，完整呈现这条有名的语义翻转链（用力 → 肯定 → 不容易 → 几乎不），原路径一跳直达今义。
mechanism_sentence 重写为翻转机制。
evidence: Etymonline: "c. 1200, "in a hard manner, with great exertion or effort," from Old English heardlice "sternly, severely, harshly; bravely; excessively""
Etymonline: "Hence "assuredly, certainly" (early 14c.). Main modern sense of "barely, just" (1540s) reverses this, via the intermediate meaning "not easily, with trouble" (early 15c.)."
hardly.mechanism_sentence: hardly 本是「使劲地、十足地」：经「费力、不容易」这道桥，1540 年代起翻成了几乎反义的「几乎不」——英语里有名的意思大翻身。

semantic_path.how: 最早见载的意思
「使足了劲」顺势引申为「十足、肯定」：14 世纪初 hardly 有『assuredly, certainly（无疑地）』义（Etymonline 编年）——劲头够大，话就说得够满。
翻面的桥在这里：「做起来用力」就是「做起来不容易」——15 世纪初 hardly 添了『not easily, with trouble（费力地、好不容易）』义（Etymonline 明说今义经此中间义而来），重心从『劲大』滑向『难成』。
「不容易有」再收一步就是「几乎没有」：1540 年代起 hardly 定型为『barely, just（几乎不）』——和最初的「十足地」几乎成了反义（Etymonline 原文用 reverses 形容这一步）。

changes: original_meaning 与首站对齐为「使恢复完整（治愈，拯救）」，点明 hælan 的字面机制『使完整』（Etymonline：literally 'to make whole'）；链 gloss 里的『问候，致敬』是 Wiktionary 所记古英语旁义，不属治愈主线，未进原义。
semantic_path 补 14 世纪末不及物『愈合』义一站（Etymonline 编年），替换套话。
mechanism_sentence 重写为与 whole 同源的说明。
evidence: Etymonline: "Old English hælan "cure; save; make whole, sound and well,"... literally "to make whole" (from PIE *kailo- "whole;" see health). Intransitive sense from late 14c."
Oxford: "Old English hǣlan (in the sense 'restore to sound health'), of Germanic origin... also to whole."
heal.mechanism_sentence: heal 字面就是「使完整」——它和 whole 是同根亲戚：病和伤都是身上「缺了一块」，治好，就是把人重新拼回完整。

semantic_path.how: 最早见载的意思
14 世纪末起 heal 长出不及物用法：主语从治病的医生换成伤口自己——不是『被治好』，而是『自己长好、愈合』（Etymonline：Intransitive sense from late 14c.）。「使完整」的动作，落到了伤口自己头上。

changes: original_meaning 由义项并列收为古英语 heorð 的核心义「炉膛，生火的地方」。
semantic_path 第二站 how 写明其转指『家』在古英语时代已出现（Etymonline 明注 OE also in transferred use 'house, home, fireside'），并非现代新义，替换套话。
mechanism_sentence 重写。
evidence: Etymonline: "Old English heorð "hearth, fireplace, part of a floor on which a fire is made," also in transferred use "house, home, fireside," from Proto-Germanic *hertha- "burning place""
hearth.mechanism_sentence: hearth 在古英语里既是生火的炉膛，也早就转指了「家」：一家人围着火坐的地方，天生就是家的代名词。

semantic_path.how: 最早见载的意思
转指在古英语时代就完成了：heorð 当时已用来指「家、炉边」（Etymonline 注 OE also in transferred use 'house, home, fireside'）——生火处即一家人聚处；今天它仍指壁炉的炉床，并保留着「家」的暖意。

changes: original_meaning 与古英语 hǣtu 首要 gloss 对齐为「热，热度」。
semantic_path 补 1660 年代『比赛一轮』义一站及其 14 世纪末的比喻前身（Etymonline 编年），替换套话。
mechanism_sentence 重写。
evidence: Etymonline: "Old English hætu, hæto "heat, warmth, quality of being hot; fervor, ardor""
Etymonline: "Meaning "a single course in a race," especially a horse race, is from 1660s, perhaps from earlier figurative sense of "violent action; a single intense effort" (late 14c.)"
heat.mechanism_sentence: heat 在古英语里就兼着「热」与「热切」：后来连一轮比赛那股热火朝天的冲劲也归了它——1660 年代起，一轮预赛就叫 a heat。

semantic_path.how: 最早见载的意思
「热」先在比喻里指一股猛劲：14 世纪末已有『violent action; a single intense effort（一次猛烈的发力）』的用法；1660 年代起，这股「一次全力以赴」落到赛场上，heat 专指比赛的一轮、预赛的一组（Etymonline 编年）。

中古英语一步（抓住→告知）的桥接来源未交代，已如实留白，计入机制留白数。
mechanism_sentence 重写为『抛出去让人抓的话』这一原文自带的核心意象。
evidence: Etymonline: "hint (n.) c. 1600 (Shakespeare), "an indirect suggestion intended to be caught by the knowing," apparently from obsolete hent, from Middle English hinten "to tell, inform" (c. 1400), from Old English hentan "to seize""
Etymonline: "OED dates the sense "small piece of practical information" to 1777."
Oxford: "apparently from obsolete hent 'grasp, get hold of', from Old English hentan... The basic notion is "something that may be taken advantage of"."
hint.mechanism_sentence: hint 的祖先 hentan 是「抓住」：暗示正是抛出去让人「抓」的话——Etymonline 给它的定义就是「说给能抓住的人听的间接提醒」。

semantic_path.how: 最早见载的意思
来源未交代这一步是怎么变的：中古英语 hinten（约 1400 年）已作「告知、透露」用，但从『抓住』到『告知』中间的桥接，三家来源都没有说明。
semantic_path.period: 中古英语时期（约 1400 年）

semantic_path.how: 名词 hint 约 1600 年见载，定义就是「抛给懂的人去抓的间接提醒」（Etymonline 原文 'an indirect suggestion intended to be caught by the knowing'）——『抓』的老影子还在：不明说，话递出去，对方自己抓住；1777 年起又添了「小贴士」义（OED 年代）。

changes: original_meaning 保留古英语 hās 的「沙哑的」。
semantic_path 第二站 how 由套话改为实质说明：义未动而形变（-r- 为约 1400 年出现的非词源插入，Etymonline 明注 unetymological）。
mechanism_sentence 重写，点明『义没变、拼写添了 r』这一真实变化，并保留来源对更早义『干、粗』的推测语气。
evidence: Etymonline: "late 14c., hors, earlier hos, from Old English has "hoarse,"... perhaps originally meaning "dried out, rough." The unetymological -r- is difficult to explain; it is first attested c. 1400"
Oxford: "Old English hās, of Germanic origin... The spelling with r was influenced in Middle English by an Old Norse cognate."
hoarse.mechanism_sentence: hoarse 是个意思没挪窝、拼写却变了的词：古英语 hās 就指嗓音沙哑（推测更早指「干、发粗」），中古英语里添了个来历不明的 r，成了今天的样子。

semantic_path.how: 最早见载的意思
词义一动没动，动的是拼写：古英语作 hās，中古英语先作 hos/hors，约 1400 年起添上一个词源上讲不通的 r（Etymonline 称为 unetymological -r-，或许与某个未见载的古英语变体 *hars 有关；牛津则说受古诺尔斯语同源词影响）。

mechanism_sentence 重写。
evidence: Etymonline: "hump (n.) 1680s (in hump-backed), of uncertain origin; perhaps from Dutch homp "lump," from Middle Low German hump "bump""
Oxford: "early 18th cent.: probably related to Low German humpe 'hump', also to Dutch homp, Low German humpe 'lump, hunk (of bread)'."
hump.mechanism_sentence: hump 来历还没有定论，多半来自荷兰语 homp、低地德语 hump「隆起的一块」：1680 年代英语先拿它说驼背，后来就专指背上那座隆起——驼峰。

changes: original_meaning 由循环定义式的「氢」改为造词时的本义「生水者」：氢是 1787 年的新造术语，其『原义』就是造词者给的构词义（Etymonline：so called because it forms water when exposed to oxygen）。
semantic_path 第二站 how 说明『造词即定名、无语义漂移』，并改正现行 mechanism_sentence 把它称作『直接传下来的老词』的错误说法。
mechanism_sentence 重写为造词机制。
evidence: Etymonline: "hydrogen (n.)... 1791, hydrogene, from French hydrogène (Modern Latin hydrogenium), coined 1787 by G. de Morveau, Lavoisier, Berthollet, and Fourcroy from Greek hydr-, stem of hydor "water" + French -gène "producing." So called because it forms water when exposed to oxygen."
Oxford: "coined in French from Greek hudro- 'water' + -genēs '-born, of a specified kind'"
hydrogen.mechanism_sentence: hydrogen 是 1787 年拉瓦锡等化学家现造的词：hydro-「水」加 -gène「生」——这种气体遇氧就生成水，所以得名「生水者」。
hydrogen.original_meaning: 生水者（遇氧能生成水的气体）

semantic_path.meaning: 生水者（遇氧能生成水的气体）

mechanism_sentence 由罗列式改为构词 + 双域（空间/时间）说明。
evidence: Etymonline: "early 15c., "with nothing interposed; direct," also with reference to time, "without delay, instant," from Old French immediat (14c.), from Late Latin immediatus "without anything between""
Oxford: "late Middle English (in the sense 'nearest in space or order'): from Old French immediat, or from late Latin immediatus, from in- 'not' + mediatus 'intervening'"
immediate.mechanism_sentence: immediate 是 in-「不」加 mediatus「居中的」拼的：中间什么都不隔——空间上不隔是「紧挨着」，时间上不隔就是「立即」。

changes: original_meaning 由「影响」补全为意大利语 influenza 的原义「（星辰的）影响，笼罩」，点明占星义背景（Etymonline：originally 'visitation, influence (of the stars)'）。

mechanism_sentence 重写。
evidence: Etymonline: "1743, borrowed (during an outbreak of the disease in Europe), from Italian influenza "influenza, epidemic," originally "visitation, influence (of the stars)"... Used in Italian for diseases at least since 1504... on notion of astral, occult, or atmospheric influence."

negative.mechanism_sentence: negative 出自拉丁语 negare「说不」：先是「否定」，1560 年代添了「消极」，又被数学借去当「负数」、被电学借去当「负电」，1853 年落到明暗颠倒的「底片」上——一路都是「正的反面」。

名词『成套』义另有来路（Etymonline set (n.1)）：中古 sette 本指『宗教群体、派别』（与 sect 同源、经法语 sette『序列』），在 set 的拼写下被重新读作『摆在一起的一组东西』，1560 年代定型为『配套使用的整套器物』——词库名词义即此。

evidence: Etymonline: "sine (n.)... 1590s... from Latin sinus "fold in a garment, bend, curve, bosom"... evidence: Etymonline: "late 14c., "free choice, freedom to do as one chooses," from Old French liberte "freedom, liberty, free will" (14c.), from Latin libertatem (nominative libertas) "civil or political freedom, condition of a free man; absence of restraint; permission," from liber "free""

Etymonline: "At first of persons; of communities, "state of being free from arbitrary, despotic, or autocratic rule or control" is by late 15c. The meaning "unrestrained action, conduct, or expression" (1550s) led to take liberties "go beyond the bounds of propriety" (1620s)."
Oxford: "late Middle English: from Old French liberte, from Latin libertas, from liber ‘free’."
liberty.mechanism_sentence: liberty 是拉丁语 libertas「自由民的状态」：经法语进英语，先是一个人的自主，后扩到不受专制的自由——过界的那一分，就是 take liberties 里的「擅自」。
liberty.original_meaning: 自由（自由民的身份与状态）

semantic_path.how: 最早见载的意思
semantic_path.meaning: 自由（自由民的身份与状态）

semantic_path.how: 14 世纪末英语借入时指个人『想做什么就做什么』的自主；15 世纪末扩到共同体——一城一国不受专制统治的状态（Etymonline 编年）：自由的单位从一个人放大到一群人。
semantic_path.meaning: 自由，自主（个人与共同体的）

semantic_path.how: 『不受约束』越界就是放纵：1550 年代起 liberty 添了贬义的一边，1620 年代 take liberties 定型为『越礼、擅自作主』——自由的影子面（Etymonline 编年）。
